title: Cryptocurrency - Industry & News Discussion
body:
O.P.
Since the advanced (general) discussion thread was shutdown, we're encouraged to make threads that are more focused on their topics.
This thread is for discussing the industry & news around the cryptocurrency space, topics things like regulation, socioeconomic factors, technological concepts and the narratives that are attached, market makers and shakers e.g. institutions, whales, organisations, and more.
An example of this would be discussing the Terra Luna debacle, and how this effected the industry and market, discussing other big players in the industry and news around them such as Tether, Coinbase or Celsius, or how the most recent regulatory bill out of the US might affect the industry.
Since we left the discussion last time, there were a few things going on:
Coinbase was making job offers, and then rescinding them
Tether had been unpegged from the dollar (and still is) and went through some $10+bn redemptions
Celcius had been looking like it may go down or implode after huge dips and unsustainable yields
Apparently Do Kwon cashed out $80m a month prior to the LUNA crash (Terra employees reported to the SEC)
US Senators introduced a new crypto bill
Think some element of price discussion will be natural here, but should be linked to a development within the industry as we already have a few pure price action threads.
Does anyone know how the new bill affects the crypto industry? Is it positive, negative, or neither?

[User #937891335 postsmunchnever odd or evenWhirlpool Enthusiast] Yea Cobba! writes...
Could have something to do with Staked ETH peg to Ethereum?
stETH is not pegged to ETH. There is no peg mechanism for it. It's purely market dynamics that determine the price.
Once you lock ETH in for stETH you cannot redeem it back for ETH (not until the merge anyway, then there's a queue based on how many redemptions are done)
If anything stETH should be trading at a discount to ETH considering the risks. Look at other ETH staking tokens like BETH (Binance ETH) and Ankr ETH to see that they have basically been always trading at a discount to ETH. It should never trade over 1:1 though because you can just mint stETH for ETH and sell it if that's the case. Arbitrage is only possible 1 way pre-merge
Keep in mind that Celsius also raised $750mil for their Series B, and I think they have a sizable loan from Tether. Rumour has it that they have dealt with FTX (Alameda) for an OTC deal to sell stETH, which would explain the dumping of ETH
